items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: Captain Donoghé, one note from the other.

ctx.x: I'm just wondering if you ever played many things for churches, you know, you mentioned being a mason. For the Shriners? Yeah. Well I played the Muslim ball every year.

I played all the Masonic balls and many others that were not Masonic. I played Clough Knight Revelers, Proteus, Harlekins. I played on the average of thirty-five carnival balls a season. Get through at twelve o'clock and rush to the hotel and play one to four and then have rehearsal next morning, nine o'clock and everybody's knocked out and they're in a bad humor. Captain Donoghé, one note from the other. I used to have to tell them, who's the musician here, you or me? I can get enough of them. Then they say he's…
Then he gives me a $100 tip.
